text.p: Tallinna Farma, a pharmaceuticals plant, said on Monday it has revised its profit forcast upwards to 48.1 million kroons from a previous forecast of 38.5 million kroons.
In a statement, the company also said that the board approved an increased forecast for it sales volume from 200 million kroons to 232 million kroons.
The company said that the change in its forcasts was due to improved sale prospects to Russia.
"The cheaper customs duties will have a positive influence on the financial results," Priit Kivi, Farma's chief executive officer, said in the statement.
Last week the company said that it had secured agreement with the Russian customs office for a reduced duty of 0.15 percent of the value of goods exported to Russia.
The company also said they had received certification from the Russian health ministry as a producer of medicial products.
